system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:41 UTC, ivy.chen launched PowerShell from Explorer to compress \\FILE-NWD-01\Shared\Clients into C:\Users\ivy.chen\AppData\Local\Temp\c.zip; Sysmon recorded creation of that archive.
At 13:44 UTC, ivy.chen launched Edge to quickshare-drop.net, a file-sharing service not listed among the organization's approved services.

At 13:48 UTC, Edge, under ivy.chen's account, sent approximately 51 MB through the proxy tunnel to quickshare-drop.net:443; Zeek independently records approximately 51 MB of client-to-proxy bytes for the connection.
The close sequence of archiving the Clients share, opening an unapproved file-sharing site, and sending a large outbound transfer strongly supports likely exfiltration of organizational data.
A separate executable named KB5034441_update.exe ran from C:\Windows\Temp under ivy.chen's account; the available records do not establish its legitimacy or purpose.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy and Zeek records show tunnel endpoints, byte counts, and timing, but do not expose the encrypted HTTPS payload or identify which local file, if any, was uploaded.
The supplied records do not include file-server audit evidence tying the archive's contents to files accessed or transferred.
The stated WS-NBLAKE-01 winsec and Sysmon collection outage from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC does not cover WS-ICHEN-01, the host involved in the observed transfer.
claims_not_established: That c.zip was the file uploaded, or that its contents account for the outbound bytes.
The exact data sent, whether the transfer completed successfully at the application level, or who controlled the destination service.
Whether ivy.chen had authorization or a legitimate business reason for the archive or transfer.
Whether KB5034441_update.exe is malicious or related to the outbound transfer.
additional_evidence_needed: Acquire and preserve c.zip, determine its contents and hash, and compare it with file-server access/audit records for the Clients share.
Collect browser history, upload-related browser artifacts, and any available proxy TLS inspection, URL, or application-level records to confirm the uploaded object and destination.
Investigate quickshare-drop.net, including domain ownership, reputation, and any service-side upload/account records available.
Acquire and analyze KB5034441_update.exe, including its hash, signature, origin, and execution artifacts.
Confirm with ivy.chen and the relevant data owner whether the archive and transfer were authorized.
